rationale: Evidence: 60 development trials across iterations 0, 2, 3 and 4 gave 2 finishes, both on the oval at base_speed 1.0. Every other run left the line at progress 0.04 to 0.16. The best design so far (iteration 4, score 129) moved the sensors forward to y=0.07 and widened the span to +/-0.05 m. That raised s-bend progress to 0.156 and slalom progress to 0.10, so the forward sensor placement helps. Speed and gain changes alone did not move the failure point, which suggests the sensing geometry is the main limit. Changes: (1) sensors moved to y=0.08, the maximum allowed, so the correction starts earlier; (2) seven sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.02 m steps, with 16 mm footprints overlapping neighbours, so the tape stays under at least one sensor at larger offsets and the signal is less saturated; (3) weights set to 33*x (-2.0, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2.0), so the signal stays near 33 times the lateral offset within the +/-2 limit; (4) kp raised to 4.5 to keep steering authority per cm similar to the iteration 4 gain; ki 0.5 and kd 0.6 kept to correct the motor mismatch and damp the swing; (5) base_speed kept at 1.0, which finished 2 of 20 oval trials. Expected result: fewer off-track exits, progress above 0.2 on the s-bend and slalom, and more oval completions. Completion on every track is not expected yet. If the robot still exits at a fixed point, the next race should point to the line-loss handling or the kd term.
